questions.stem: You are a medical student and today your examination scheme came. You decided to go to the library today. While going to the library you were carrying a stack of books. On the way, your friend saw you and placed another large book on top of the stack. Which of the following best describes how the skeletal muscle compensates for the increase in the load being carried?

options.label: A
options.text: Decrease muscle length below the resting length

options.label: B
options.text: Increase muscle length beyond the resting length

options.label: C
options.text: Increase the number of motor units activated

questions.answerText: Increase the number of motor units activated
questions.solutionHtml:
Increase the number of motor units activated

As a greater force of contraction is required so more motor units should be activated to produce enough force of contraction. So the correct answer is C.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.80.

questions.stem: The motion of the endolymph in the semicircular canals when the head is held still will result in the perception of :
questions.solutionHtml:
Continued rotation
  • Rotational acceleration in the plane of a given semicircular canal stimulates its crista.
  • The endolymph, because of its inertia, is displaced in a direction opposite to the direction of rotation.

 



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 214-15.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a preganglionic sympathetic neurotransmitter?
questions.solutionHtml:
Acetylcholine

The preganglionic neurotransmitter is acetylcholine (nicotinic) and the postganglionic neurotransmitter (at effector organs) is noradrenaline (norepinephrine), except at sweat glands (muscarinic acetylcholine).



Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 586.

questions.stem: The precentral gyrus and corticospinal tract are essential for which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Voluntary movement

These structures are essential for the generation of fine voluntary movements.

 



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 202–205.

questions.stem: Which of the following is involved in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lower motor neuron

An example of a disease that leads to lower motor neuron damage is amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 244.

β3 adrenergic receptor & UCP1

Activation of either β(1)-adrenergic receptors or β(3)-adrenergic receptors were able to increase UCP1 mRNA and protein levels. Thus, in humans, β(1)-adrenergic receptors could play an important role in regulating nonshivering thermogenesis.
